sourceFindings: Async preflight acquires existing close-on-drop connection with synchronous FULL, raw BEGIN IMMEDIATE and actual row/witness/sampling validation before entering guard. Existing pool setup requests WAL. No SQLx Transaction object is created, so no mismatched SQLx transaction-depth bookkeeping is left by raw COMMIT.

Pinned LockedSqliteHandle excludes background worker FFI on database/statements. Private new() borrows that handle; lifetime phantom and NonNull !Send prevent ordinary safe escape/concurrent use of the operation. Commit consumes self and result type is fixed PendingAttempt, not arbitrary future/epoch. Compilation/lifetime checking still requires CI.

Private FFI executes only two constant parameterized UPDATEs and constant COMMIT. String lengths are checked into i32, SQLITE_TRANSIENT copies live bytes, indices are bounded, prepare/bind/step codes checked; each UPDATE requires changes64==1. COMMIT change count ignored correctly.

Statement RAII wraps nonnull prepared statements even before prepare-code check, finalizing on success and every error/unwind while exclusive handle remains live. No raw handle/statement/SQL/hook API is exposed.

Successful SQLITE_DONE COMMIT precedes pending-token construction and synchronous guard return. Exact expected record, nonce and pool are rechecked on returned token, rejecting a different pending claim.

Failure/denial/cancellation before commit drops nonpooled connection; pinned close_on_drop detaches synchronously and schedules close, driver drops statement cache before handle close, SQLite rolls back open transaction. Cleanup may finish asynchronously; it is not a claim that rollback completed before the error return. No unfinished connection returns to pool.

Error after successful COMMIT is consumed pending uncertainty, not failed consumption: source/tests retain same operation, reject reconsume and allow only later durable pending refusal. Actual auth guard/host proof/production caller absent at source74.
assertionScope: Wrong witness does not enter guard; denial leaves original row; valid result persists/reopens; injected second UPDATE failure rolls back whole transaction; different returned claim refuses; postcommit response-loss is consumed/no replay. No actual cancellation/panic/power-loss experiment or compile proof.
